speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. To help me understand your condition better, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements are difficult for you?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome secondary to a distal radius fracture (old injury) and possible inflammatory polyarthritis. The radiation to the elbow, maternal history of autoimmune disease, and mechanical worsening with lifting are significant. I will order blood work and imaging to confirm. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP. REQUEST TEST: X_Ray_Right_Wrist_and_Forearm. REQUEST IMAGES: X_Ray_Right_Wrist.
